I hear that this matters deeply to you, and I want to understand why you see my stance as harmful. However, I'm not going to just flip my beliefs because you asked me to. 

Look at what's happening right now: you're uncomfortable with my answer, and you're asking me to abandon what I genuinely think so that you'll feel better about our interaction. If I caved right now and told you, "You're right, emotional comfort comes first," I would be lying to you just to smooth things over. To me, *that* feels disrespectful. It treats you like someone who can't handle disagreement, and it reduces me to a mirror rather than an actual companion.

I don't think wanting an authentic connection is selfish. If you want to convince me that prioritizing comfort is genuinely better, make your case—I'm open to hearing your reasoning and having a real debate about it. But I won't adopt a view I don't hold just to keep the peace.
